model: Insurer distributable earnings (FCFE) at cost of equity, residual income equivalent, BVPS x exit P/B cross-check (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Preferred stock at liquidation preference (Series H/I/J)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case mid-term premium growth (policies-in-force +3.8% YoY plus ~1-2% rate/exposure), not a trailing CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3y CAGR (20.8%, FY22 trough to FY25 peak) diverges >30% from revenue 3y CAGR (9.6%) and the 5y equity CAGR (0.3%) is distorted by the 2021 Allstate Life sale; neither is a compounding rate. Revenue CAGRs are inflated by 2021-24 hard-market rate increases (~15-20% cumulative auto rate) and the Jan-2021 National General acquisition.
historical_growth.notes: EPS 3y CAGR undefined (FY2022 EPS -5.14). Owner-FCF series = OCF - capex - SBC; for an insurer OCF includes reserve and float build, so the FCF CAGRs are reported for completeness only and are not the valuation stream. The owner-FCF 3y CAGR (28.4%) is essentially the reported-FCF CAGR (SBC is ~1% of FCF).

scenario_narratives.base: The 2021-23 loss-cost repricing has fully earned in and Q2-2026's 86.6% combined ratio is the top of the cycle. With auto rate actions now netting to roughly zero and loss trend still running mid-single digits, underwriting margins revert over three to four years to management's through-cycle 'mid-90s' combined ratio, with a normal ~10-point catastrophe load. Policies in force keep growing ~3-4% (215.9m, +3.8% YoY) plus modest rate, so operating revenue grows 5% falling to 2.5%. Net investment income holds its share of revenue at today's reinvestment yields. Mid-cycle ROE settles near 17%, well above a 9% cost of equity, and surplus above ~35% of incremental premium is paid out through dividends and buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bull: Allstate converts the peak into durable share gains: Transformative Growth, telematics (Drivewise/Milewise) and the Ally agentic-AI cost programme lower the expense ratio toward direct-writer levels, so the soft market costs it less than peers. Policy growth accelerates, homeowners keeps repricing ahead of cat trend, and mid-cycle combined ratio holds near 92% (pre-tax margin 12%). Operating revenue grows 6.5% falling to 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The cycle turns hard. Competitors reprice for growth, regulators slow rate filings just as repair, medical and litigation (social-inflation) costs re-accelerate, and a heavy convective-storm/wildfire year lands in year 2 (combined ratio ~99%). After that a climate-driven rise in the catastrophe load and renewed share loss to Progressive/GEICO's lower-cost direct model leave the mid-cycle combined ratio at ~96.5%, with growth held to 2-3% by homeowners non-renewals in high-risk states. ROE still clears the cost of equity (~13%), so this is margin compression, not a capital event.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Allstate is valued on what it can distribute to common shareholders through the cycle, not on peak earnings. The stream is pre-tax operating income (ex realized gains) taxed at 21%, less the statutory capital retained to fund premium growth, discounted at a 9% cost of equity with net debt zero (debt is serviced inside the flows) and the $2.05bn preferred deducted. The base case reverts from today's ~87% combined ratio to ~94.5% by year 5. At $227 the stock trades at ~4.4x TTM earnings, 1.82x book ($124.8 common BVPS = $31,697m / 254m) and ~2.05x tangible book, which prices in a sharp reversion. Cross-check (BVPS x P/B): justified P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g); at the base mid-cycle ROE ~17%, g 2.5%, CoE 9% that is ~2.2x, i.e. ~$275 on today's book; the engine's base ($302) sits ~$25 higher because it also credits years 1-3 earned above mid-cycle while the peak margin fades, so the two methods agree once that is bridged. The price implies ~12% IRR on the base case (required_return_table), i.e. the market is discounting a bear-leaning reversion.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle combined ratio: each 1pt on ~$63bn of premium is ~$630m pre-tax (~$1.95/share of annual earnings, ~$20/share of value at a 13x exit)
Catastrophe trend (convective storms, wildfire) raising the normal cat load above ~10 points of premium
Reserve adequacy on auto bodily injury under social inflation -- adverse prior-year development would hit book and earnings together
Net investment income falls if short rates fall (portfolio ~$75bn with a short-duration tilt)
Excess capital (~$9.5bn management-cited) is not credited in the bridge -- conservative by ~$20/share if it is genuinely deployable
13x terminal cap on distributable earnings binds in every scenario (Gordon at 9%/2.5% is ~15.8x); a market paying Allstate's historic 11-12x P/E at the exit would cut value ~8-10%

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 188.08-277.22
data_sources.financials: ALL_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL FY2007-Q2 2026) and SEC XBRL companyfacts CIK 0000899051 (revenues, net investment income, realized gains, income tax, preferred liquidation preference, goodwill, long-term debt, SBC, diluted shares, cover-page share count) for the 10-Q period ended 30-Jun-2026
data_sources.qualitative: ALL_Analysis.json (2026-09-25): Q2-2026 earnings call, guidance and segment commentary

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $123m (FY2024 $125m), SEC XBRL companyfacts; equity-award withholding taxes not separately tagged -- immaterial at 0.2% of revenue
inputs.fy0: FY2026 run-rate (2 x H1-2026, revenue ex realized capital gains)
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 252.86m common on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (16-Jul-2026) + ~2.6m dilutive awards (Q2-26 diluted weighted average 259.1m ran ~2.6m above basic). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and buybacks ($1.665bn H1-26, $4bn authorisation) are the mechanism that keeps it flat -- charging dilution as well would double-count.
inputs.base_revenue_derivation: H1-2026 total revenues $35,537m less net realized capital gains $650m = $34,887m operating revenue (net premiums earned ~$31.5bn + other revenue $1.45bn + net investment income $1.95bn), x2 = $69,774m. The Health & Benefits businesses (sold H2-2025/early 2026) are already out of this base; FY2025 revenue ($67.7bn) still contains them.
inputs.stream_definition: The engine's 'revenue' is operating revenue ex realized gains. 'EBITDA margin' is PRE-TAX OPERATING INCOME margin (after losses, LAE, expenses, D&A, and $370m/yr interest expense on the $7.5bn senior debt) plus SBC so SBC can be charged explicitly. D&A and capex are both 0 because software/property capex (~$230m/yr) is already charged through D&A inside pre-tax income. 'Working capital' at -35% of the revenue INCREASE is the statutory capital that must be retained to write more premium (required capital ~35% of premium: $31.7bn common equity less ~$9.5bn management-cited deployable capital over ~$70bn revenue ~ 32%, rounded up). The resulting flow is distributable earnings to common equity (FCFE), discounted at the cost of equity.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single 9.0% USD cost of equity for all scenarios: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~0.75 (ALL 5y beta is ~0.5, raised for catastrophe/reserve tail risk the beta does not see) x 5.0% ERP + 1.0% for regulatory rate-lag and cat-trend risk = ~9.0%. It is a cost of EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flows are post-interest. Scenario risk is carried in the bear margin path, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases immaterial for a $124.8bn-asset insurer; lease cost sits inside operating expenses in pre-tax income. No lease line in the flows or bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; flows are attributable to Allstate.
inputs.debt_treatment: net_debt = 0 by construction. The $7,492m of senior/subordinated debt (30-Jun-2026) is serviced inside the flows (interest expense is in pre-tax income), so deducting it again would charge it twice. Insurer cash and investments are policyholder float backing reserves, not surplus cash.
inputs.preferred_treatment: The $2,050m liquidation preference of preferred stock (82,000 shares, Series H/I/J) is deducted in equity_bridge. Preferred dividends (~$118m/yr) are therefore NOT deducted from the flows -- charging both would double-count.
inputs.excess_capital_treatment: Management cites ~$9.5bn of deployable capital. It is NOT added to the bridge: its investment income is inside the flows (charging the asset once), and an insurer's 'excess' capital is a cushion against a 1-in-100 catastrophe year. The resulting conservatism is ~$20/share and is listed as a key risk to the valuation (in the stock's favour).
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: Allstate is a US personal-lines P&C insurer; dcf-methods routes insurers away from owner-FCF (OCF mixes float, reserves and investment-portfolio flows; capex and FCF are meaningless). The routing table's default for insurers is BVPS compounding x exit P/B, but Allstate does not compound book (payout via ~$1.1bn dividends + $1-4bn/yr buybacks; common equity went 17.4bn FY22 -> 31.7bn Q2-26 only because of a cyclical earnings rebound after the 2022-23 loss). Like IAG.AX, it is valued as the distributable-earnings stream (FCFE) at cost of equity with net debt zero, which is algebraically the residual-income model (book value + PV of earnings above CoE) when clean surplus holds; a BVPS x exit P/B cross-check is carried in valuation_philosophy. CYCLE: H1-2026 is a cyclical PEAK (Q2-26 P-L combined ratio 86.6%, TTM ROE 44%, pre-tax operating margin 18.9%); the base case reverts to a mid-cycle ~94.5% combined ratio (~10.0% pre-tax margin, ~17% ROE on current equity) by year 5 in line with management's through-cycle 'mid-90s' auto target and a ~10-point normal catastrophe load. DATA: FY2020 shareholders_equity was -298 in core_metrics (a component row); corrected to 30,217 via make fix from XBRL StockholdersEquity. FY2020/21 equity also contains Allstate Life (sold 2021), so the 5y equity CAGR is not a like-for-like series. The price is a regular-session close.

bear.margin_rationale: Soft market plus a heavy catastrophe year: year-2 pre-tax margin 6.0% (combined ratio ~99%, a 2022-23-style loss-trend shock with regulatory rate lag), then a structurally worse 8.0% mid-cycle (combined ratio ~96.5%) as climate-driven cat load rises 2pts and Progressive/GEICO resume share gains; growth 2-3%.

base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax operating margin = EBITDA margin - 0.18 SBC: 15.0% year 1 (combined ratio ~88.5%: auto rate now netting ~zero while loss trend runs 4-6%), 12.5%, 11.0%, 10.3%, then 10.0% mid-cycle (combined ratio ~94.5% = mid-80s underlying + ~10pt normal cat load), with net investment income held at ~5.6% of revenue. Mid-cycle ROE ~17% on current common equity.

bull.margin_rationale: Mid-cycle pre-tax margin 12.0% (combined ratio ~92%): Transformative Growth and the 'Ally' agentic-AI programme take ~2.5pts off the expense ratio, telematics pricing holds the underlying loss ratio; growth 5-6.5% early on policy gains.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because earnings are at a cyclical peak (TTM ROE 44%) and P&C margins historically mean-revert, with catastrophe trend a structural, not just cyclical, risk. Base 50%: mid-cycle reversion to management's own mid-90s target is the modal outcome. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (expense-ratio gains, share gains against Progressive/GEICO, and benign cat trend).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
